name: Firmus GEE01 / Long Reach Data Centre (Bell Bay)
notes: 'AI factory' campus proposed at Lot 1 East Tamar Highway, Long Reach, Bell Bay (former Gunns pulp mill site): two purpose-built AI data halls plus office and maintenance workshop; ~288MW draw with direct-to-chip liquid cooling; three 220kV TasNetworks transmission lines cross the site. Development application lodged with George Town Council (June 2026); community consultation extended after backlash; DA requests ~19.2 ML/yr water from TasWater. Status: DA under assessment - planned (grade B). Capacity basis: campus draw, not IT load.

name: Energy Estate Digital Bell Bay data centre hub
notes: Announcement (Dec 2025): Bell Bay is the first of three planned Tasmania data centre hubs (CaliNewy subsea cable lands at Bell Bay); MOU with H2U Group for renewable supply and common-user infrastructure. No DA, operator or facility scope verified - lead only (grade C).

name: DXN TAS01 (ex-TasmaNet DC2/DC3) colocation data centre
developer: DXN Limited (TAS01 Pty Ltd), sold to DADT
notes: Tier II modular colocation facility at 40-50 Innovation Drive, Dowsing Point (Tasmanian Technopark, City of Glenorchy LGA; marketed as 'Hobart data centre'); ~30-35 racks with capacity to expand to ~100; serves Tasmanian government agencies and enterprise. Acquired by DXN from TasmaNet in 2020 (AU$2.7m); DXN sold TAS01 to DADT effective 30 June 2026 (landlord consent pending); purchaser continues operating.

name: DXN TAS01 modular expansion capacity
notes: DXN FY21 annual report states TAS01 has capacity to triple its current capacity under its current approved development approval without interrupting services, due to modular construction. Confirms an existing approved DA covers expansion of the Dowsing Point site (grade B, ASX filing).

name: Firmus Wesley Vale AI factory
notes: Firmus lodged a development application for an AI factory at Wesley Vale (Latrobe municipality, northern Tasmania); community drop-in sessions held in Latrobe and Moriarty (July 2026); company proposed using Tasmanian Irrigation scheme water, which Tasmanian Irrigation denied (agriculture/hydrogen purpose only). Capacity not yet disclosed; DA under assessment - planned (grade B).

name: Firmus LST01 data centre campus
notes: 20MW colocation/HPC data centre in Launceston (potential up to 40MW); immersion liquid cooling up to 100kW/rack, PUE ~1.03, renewable-powered; grid demand-response via DRADIS. A second 20MW hall (LST02) was planned at the same campus (target mid-2022 per source); status of LST02 not re-verified (grade B, DCD).

name: Firmus Project Southgate AI Factory (St Leonards)
notes: AI Factory campus at St Leonards (5 ha; two server halls, office and associated infrastructure), endorsed/approved by Launceston City Council (Sep 2025); Stage 1a 44MW by 2026 (AU$2.1bn investment), Stage 1b doubles to 90MW; further ~300MW Stage 2 planned subject to final approvals; renewable-powered; reported scalable to ~400MW. capacity_mw = Stage 1 combined 90MW (grade B, DCD + The Mercury).
